claim:
For \(\lambda>1\), let \(R_\lambda^2=(\mathbb R^2,N_\lambda)\) be the real Banaś--Frączek plane
\[
N_\lambda(u,v)=\max\left\{\lambda|u|,\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\right\}.
\]
Its Zbăganu constant is
\[
C_Z(R_\lambda^2)=
\begin{cases}
\lambda,&1<\lambda\le\sqrt2,\\[2mm]
2\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}},&\lambda\ge\sqrt2.
\end{cases}
\]
The maximizing geometry changes sharply at \(\lambda=\sqrt2\). For \(1<\lambda<\sqrt2\), after the coordinate sign symmetries of \(N_\lambda\), exchanging the two vectors, and changing either vector sign, every maximizing pair has the form
\[
x=r\cos\alpha\,(\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha),\qquad
y=r\sin\alpha\,(-\sin\alpha,\cos\alpha),
\]
where \(r>0\) and
\[
\arccos(\lambda^{-1})\le\alpha\le\arcsin(\lambda^{-1}).
\]
At \(\lambda=\sqrt2\) this interval collapses to \(\alpha=\pi/4\). For \(\lambda>\sqrt2\), every maximizing pair is, up to the same symmetries,
\[
x=r\left(1,\sqrt{\lambda^2-1}\right),\qquad
y=r\left(-1,\sqrt{\lambda^2-1}\right),
\qquad r\ne0.
\]
Thus the low-parameter regime has a continuum of Euclidean-orthogonal extremizers, while the high-parameter regime has one transition-ray orbit whose members are not Euclidean orthogonal except at the phase point.
integrity: The proof treats all four max-branch products, optimizes an explicit quadratic minorant, supplies exact lower-bound pairs in both parameter regimes, and traces equality through every inequality. Numerical exploration was used only as a private stress test.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to the real two-dimensional Banaś--Frączek norm. It does not treat the generalized p-family. The 1993 object source was verified only to year-level public dating in the checked material, so the exact date field uses the earliest checked source with verified day-level public evidence.
title: Exact Zbăganu phase diagram of the Banaś--Frączek plane
